extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH grant applications (e.g., R01/R21) and grant writers seeking an NIH-specific proposal template
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting NIH-style research grant applications using a hypothesis-driven framework, including specific aims, significance, innovation, and approach sections and practices to maximize competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-Driven Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Every aim should test a discrete, falsifiable hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses must be supported by, but not be the same as, preliminary data. Aims should not be co-dependent (one shouldn't fail if another fails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims Page — four-paragraph structure (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the Specific Aims page into four paragraphs that introduce the problem, identify the gap, state the long-term goal and hypothesis, and list the aims with expected outcomes and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this template to produce a concise, compelling one-page summary that frames the proposal for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — Paragraph 1 (Introduction)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly situate the project in the context of what is known and why the problem matters to science or health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — Paragraph 2 (Gap/Critical need)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the knowledge gap or barrier that prevents progress and why it is important to address now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — Paragraph 3 (Goal, Hypothesis, Rationale)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the long-term objective and the central, testable hypothesis with brief rationale that links to preliminary data or theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — Paragraph 4 (Aims, Outcomes, Impact)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List discrete aims, state expected results, and explain the likely impact or advance if aims are achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance Section Template
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the importance of the problem, identify critical barrier(s) to progress, explain how your project addresses these barriers, and state the expected positive impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize public health/scientific importance and how the project will move the field forward by removing specific barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight novel concepts, novel methodologies/technologies, novel applications of existing approaches, or anticipated paradigm shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state what is new compared to current practice and why that novelty matters; anticipate and describe potential paradigm-level changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach Section — structure per aim
rubrics_metrics.description: For each aim include title and overarching strategy; justification and feasibility (linked to preliminary data); research design, methods, and analysis; expected outcomes; potential problems and alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about how methods will test the hypothesis, provide evidence of feasibility (preliminary data), define analytic plans, and proactively discuss contingencies and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and Feasibility (Approach subcriterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification and feasibility must be linked to preliminary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how preliminary results or prior work make the proposed approach plausible and likely to succeed; reviewers expect this linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design, Methods, and Analysis (Approach subcriterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe research design, specific methods, and planned analyses in sufficient detail for reviewers to assess rigor and appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experimental design features that support causal inference and statistical/analytic plans that align with hypotheses and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected Outcomes (Approach subcriterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the expected outcomes for each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify what success looks like and how outcomes will inform the central hypothesis and future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Problems and Alternative Approaches (Approach subcriterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate potential problems and describe alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate foresight and flexibility; show that failure paths have been considered and that there are feasible backup plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of Experimental Design and Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve rigor of experimental design and enhance proposal transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly address experimental rigor in design choices, provide transparent reporting of methods and assumptions, and justify sample sizes, controls, and analytic approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss Strengths and Limitations of Preliminary Results and Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly discuss strengths and limitations of your preliminary results and of published literature you rely on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating critical appraisal of evidence builds credibility and helps reviewers evaluate feasibility and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a Biological Variable (SABV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and address sex as a biological variable where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how sex/gender will be considered in design, analysis, and interpretation, or justify why it is not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate key biological resources (e.g., cell lines, antibodies) used in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document provenance and validation steps to assure resource identity and reproducibility.
